Versailles' German grievances and disputed borders fed revisionist demands that Britain and France tried to satisfy at Munich with territorial concessions.
Westphalia awarded Brandenburg-Prussia Eastern Pomerania and secularized bishoprics such as Halberstadt and Minden, enlarging the state that became the Kingdom of Prussia.
Nasser pursued pan-Arab unity and accepted Syria's 1958 request for merger, creating the United Arab Republic under his leadership.
The 1952 Free Officers' revolution brought Nasser's regime to power, giving the pan-Arab union project its Egyptian base.
Jacques Cartier's 1534 voyage claimed the St. Lawrence region for France, initiating the New France claims that anchored the empire.
European overseas exploration from the late fifteenth century opened the maritime routes and trade prospects that France pursued in the Americas and beyond.
The Russian Civil War let the Red Army conquer the Democratic Republic of Georgia in 1921, establishing Soviet rule over the territory.
Centuries of division among the Northern and Southern dynasties left China fragmented, which Sui Emperor Wen reunified by conquering Chen in 589.
Li Yuan's rebellion against the overextended Sui, after failed Goguryeo campaigns, toppled the dynasty in 618 and founded the Tang.
Precise CMB measurements by COBE and WMAP tested and constrained inflationary cosmology, which had predicted the sky's observed uniformity and fluctuations.
Ichkeria's 1991 unilateral declaration of independence, rejected by Moscow, led Yeltsin to send federal troops into Chechnya in December 1994.
The Balkan Wars expanded Serbia and Bulgaria and angered Austria-Hungary, heightening the rivalries that fed the July Crisis and the outbreak of World War I.
Ottoman control of eastern trade routes after 1453 pushed Portugal and Spain to seek sea routes to Asia, accelerating overseas exploration.
Ottoman expansion after 1453 conquered the Byzantine Morea and Athens, bringing Greek lands under centuries of Ottoman rule.
Pop artists' use of everyday objects and mass-media imagery broadened what counted as art, paving the way for conceptual art in the 1960s.
Kwantung Army officers of Imperial Japan staged the 1931 Mukden Incident and then established Manchukuo as a puppet state in 1932.
Chiang Kai-shek's Northern Expedition unified much of China and threatened Japan's Manchurian interests, prompting the Kwantung Army to seize Manchuria.
Depression-era economic distress strengthened militarist factions in Tokyo that favored seizing Manchuria's resources and markets.
Manchukuo became the base from which Japan expanded into North China, leading to full-scale war with China in July 1937.
Japan's conquest of Manchuria began the militarist expansion in Asia that drew it into the Pacific War within World War II.
The Grand Duchy's nobility accepted the 1569 Union of Lublin, merging with the Kingdom of Poland into the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
Fear of French invasion and the 1798 Irish rebellion led Pitt's government to pass the 1800 Acts of Union, joining Ireland to Great Britain.
Crusaders diverted from their goal sacked Constantinople in 1204, and their leaders then carved the Byzantine lands into the Latin Empire.
Innocent III's 1198 call for a new crusade launched the expedition that ended in the 1204 conquest of Constantinople.
Byzantine exiles under Theodore Laskaris set up the Nicaean state in Anatolia, which retook Constantinople from the Latins in 1261.
Michael Komnenos Doukas founded the Despotate of Epirus after the 1204 conquest, creating a rival Greek state that contested Latin control.
The Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact's secret protocol placed Estonia in the Soviet sphere, enabling Moscow's 1940 occupation and annexation.
Repeated Mongol invasions of northwestern India pressed the Delhi sultans to maintain large standing armies and frontier fortifications.
Babur's 1526 invasion from Kabul defeated the last Lodi sultan at Panipat, founding the Mughal Empire on the sultanate's ruins.
Vijayanagara arose around 1336 as Hindu leaders resisted the southern expansion of Delhi's Muhammad bin Tughlaq, creating a rival southern empire.
Hasan Gangu's 1347 revolt against Delhi's authority established the Bahmani Sultanate, an independent Deccan kingdom.
Seljuk Turks under Tughril Beg overthrew the Buyid amirs in Baghdad in 1055, taking control of the Abbasid caliphate.
Caliph al-Qa'im invited Tughril Beg to Baghdad to end Buyid domination, granting him the sultan title and making the Seljuks protectors of the caliphate.
Seljuk conquests in Anatolia and Syria prompted Byzantine appeals that led Pope Urban II to launch the First Crusade in 1095.
Freud formulated the Oedipus complex from clinical cases and his self-analysis, presenting it in The Interpretation of Dreams.
Surrealists drew on Freudian psychoanalysis, including Oedipal themes of desire and repression, to explore the unconscious in their art and writing.
Gutenberg combined movable metal type, oil-based ink and an adapted screw press around 1439, creating a practical mechanized printing system.
Renaissance humanists' demand for classical texts and new learning created a large market that rewarded mass book production.
Cheap, fast reproduction on presses enabled regular news sheets, leading to the first periodical newspapers in the early seventeenth century.
Printed pamphlets and vernacular Bibles let Luther's writings spread quickly across Germany, underpinning the Protestant Reformation.
Mass-printed vernacular books and newspapers created shared reading publics that helped build national identities, a process historians call print capitalism.
Coriolis's 1835 analysis of motion in rotating frames supplied the mathematical basis for the rotating-wheel effects that Foucault exploited in 1852.
Gyroscopic flight instruments and autopilots allowed aircraft to fly stably without visual horizon references, making instrument flight practical.
Gyroscopes give spacecraft attitude control and orientation sensing, making reliable satellite stabilization and pointing practical.
After Germany's 1871 victory, France sought Russian support, producing the Franco-Russian alliance that later anchored the Triple Entente.
German colonial and naval ambitions alarmed Britain and France, drawing London toward Paris and St Petersburg through the 1904 and 1907 agreements.
Augustus II of Poland-Lithuania joined Russia and Denmark's 1700 alliance against Sweden, opening the war with an attack on Swedish Livonia.
Victory over Sweden and the 1721 Treaty of Nystad gave Russia the Baltic coast, and the Senate proclaimed Peter I emperor.
Prussia gained Swedish Stettin and part of Western Pomerania in the war's settlement, enlarging the state that became the Kingdom of Prussia.
Achaemenid expansion under Darius I, including the conquest of Ionia, drew Greek city-states into direct conflict with Persian power.
Atomic bombs developed and used in World War II created the proliferation problem that the NPT was designed to contain.
Nice left institutional reform unresolved before enlargement, prompting the Laeken process and convention that eventually drafted the Lisbon reforms.
Enlightenment ideals of reason and civic virtue drove artists and writers to model their work on classical antiquity.
Romantic writers and painters reacted against neoclassical rules of form and reason, emphasizing emotion, nature and the individual.
The 1282 Sicilian Vespers split the Kingdom of Sicily, leaving the Angevin rulers in control of the mainland as the Kingdom of Naples.
Ivan IV's 1558 invasion of Livonia sought Baltic access and launched a quarter-century war that drew in Poland, Lithuania and Sweden.
Muscovite pressure in the Livonian War pushed Poland and Lithuania to merge at Lublin in 1569, forming the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.
Seljuk Turks under Tughril Beg overthrew the Buyid amirs in Baghdad in 1055, becoming protectors of the Abbasid caliphate.
The Abbasid caliph invited Tughril Beg to Baghdad to end Buyid rule, granting the Seljuks legitimacy as defenders of Sunni Islam.
Seljuk conquests in Anatolia and Syria prompted Byzantine appeals that led Pope Urban II to call the First Crusade at Clermont in 1095.
After the Seljuk sultanate of Rum weakened in the thirteenth century, its successor principalities gave rise to the Ottoman state under Osman.
Graphical browsers such as NCSA Mosaic, released in 1993, applied GUI conventions to make the Web usable for ordinary people.
Solar cells powered early spacecraft such as Vanguard 1 in 1958, establishing photovoltaic arrays as the standard satellite power source.
The 1589 extinction of the Valois line made Henry of Navarre, a Bourbon, the heir to the French throne.
Philip V's Bourbon accession in 1700 brought centralizing reforms to the Spanish Empire after the War of the Spanish Succession.
The ICRC's 1863 founding and push for neutral battlefield care led to the 1864 Geneva Conference and the First Geneva Convention.
Twitter was built as a web service on the World Wide Web's browsers and protocols, which made its public real-time messaging platform possible.
Musk's 2022 acquisition of the company and its 2023 rebranding as X ended the Twitter name and platform era.
The 1894 Tonghak Rebellion in Korea prompted both Qing China and Japan to send troops there, triggering the war between them.
Empress Dowager Cixi's diversion of naval funds to palace projects left the Beiyang Fleet underequipped against Japan.
Prussia traded troops to the Habsburgs for the 1701 royal title and gained Upper Guelders at the 1713 Utrecht settlement.
Mughal control over the Deccan provoked Shivaji's revolt, the founding act of an independent Maratha polity.
Aurangzeb's long Deccan campaigns drained Mughal resources and hardened Maratha resistance under Shivaji and his successors.
Maratha chiefs such as the Bhonsles built their power serving the Deccan sultanates of Bijapur and Ahmadnagar before breaking away.
The collapse of Austria-Hungary at the end of World War I let South Slav lands unite into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1918.
The 1919–1920 Paris settlements recognized the South Slav kingdom and fixed its borders with Italy, Austria and Hungary.
The 1929 royal dictatorship and centralizing policies radicalized Croat nationalism, helping the Ustaše grow into an armed separatist movement.
Compton's 1923 demonstration that light carries momentum reinforced the photon picture on which Heisenberg's quantum framework built.
Innocent III called for a new crusade in 1198, the expedition that Venetian interests then redirected toward Constantinople.
The fall of France in June 1940 gave Germany Channel-coast airfields and made an invasion of Britain strategically possible.
Hitler's Germany planned Operation Sea Lion and launched the Luftwaffe offensive to win air superiority for an invasion of Britain.
